summary: Clarify client/server replay-suppression and acknowledgement contract for cross-SDK retries and external webhook side-effects
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports unexpected duplicate downstream webhook side-effects after client retry during intermittent network blips. Impact: DocuServe observed duplicate invoice webhook posts causing double-processing in their accounting pipeline for ~4% of requests during a 9:13–9:45 UTC window. Environment: prod (us-east), enterprise tenant on dedicated routing policy, SDKs in use: python (v1.12.0) and typescript (v0.9.4).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start long-running chat with function-tool enabled and external webhook target configured.
2) Simulate short TCP connection drop on client side (client reconnect/retry logic triggers).
3) SDK emits retry and resends the request without a clear semantic ack from Redwood for the previously-accepted func/tool execution.
4) Downstream webhook receives second POST (same payload idempotency semantics not enforced server-side).

Observed behaviour: External webhook receives the same callback twice (duplicate side-effect). Customer notes this happens more often when client network retry uses immediate reconnect (no jitter) and when requests route through an edge proxy that strips a custom X-Client-Nonce header.

Expected behaviour: One of the following: (a) SDK-level dedupe prevents resubmission when server acknowledged execution; (b) server returns a definitive non-retryable ack that client can rely on; or (c) server exposes a replay-suppression token that downstream can use to dedupe side-effects.

Temporary workaround requested by customer: Guidance on SDK configuration to add jitter/backoff, ensure client preserves nonce header, and recommend webhook-side de-dup keys until a platform-level mitigation is available.
steps_to_reproduce: Start chat session with function/tool calling and webhook target configured
Induce client TCP disconnect (short blip) and allow SDK to retry immediately
Observe duplicate POSTs to the webhook target within a 30s window
Confirm client sdk versions and edge-proxy header retention behavior

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support): Reproduced scenario in staging with an edge sidecar that canonicalizes headers; when X-Client-Nonce was removed by proxy, SDK retry produced a new nonce and server treated request as distinct. SRE found serving-runtime wrote a completed ack for the first execution (internal_id=tx-98213) but the client did not observe it due to connection drop. There is no opaque replay-suppression token exposed in the current API; server relies on client-supplied idempotency keys. Edge proxy config in customer's infra is stripping that key preflight.

Hypothesis: The platform's current contract assumes idempotency keys are preserved end-to-end. When proxies mutate headers (or when API keys are rotated mid-stream), dedupe fails. SDKs currently recommend per-request idempotency but do not enforce persisted session-scoped nonces across reconnects for streaming sessions.

SRE quick test: enabling sticky header passthrough at proxy prevented duplicates in controlled test. Code reference: platform ingress normalization codepath at router/header_normalizer.go: lines 122-145 (linked PR provided).
customer_impact_summary: Duplicates causing double ingestion of webhook events resulting in accounting reconciliation issues. Estimated duplicate rate 3–5% during intermittent network events. Customer has temporarily paused automated reconciliation and is seeking a long term mitigation.

Platform follow-up: Product/SRE to design an explicit replay-suppression token in the API and add server-side dedupe when idempotency header absent. Next steps tracked in INT-91200 and INT-84021.

public_notes: If you run into duplicates on webhook side-effects during client retries: ensure your proxies preserve idempotency headers, add client-side jitter/backoff, and consider persisting a session idempotency key in your client until the platform-level replay token is available.
